<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"><A name="Bussiness"></A>ITEM 1.&nbsp; &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></B><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">BUSINESS&nbsp;</FONT></I></B></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Overview</FONT></B></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Originally established in 1885 and incorporated in 1921, we are the largest food distributor serving military commissaries and exchanges in the United States, in terms of revenue.&nbsp;Our core businesses include distributing food to military commissaries <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">and</FONT> independent grocery retailers, and <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">distributing to and operating </FONT>our corporate-owned retail stores.&nbsp; Our sales in fiscal 2012 were approximately $4.8 billion.&nbsp;Our business currently consists of three primary operating segments: Military Food Distribution (&#8220;Military&#8221;), Food Distribution and Retail.&nbsp;Financial information about our business segments for the three most recent fiscal years is contained in Part II, Item 8 of this report under Note (18) &#8211; &#8220;Segment Information&#8221; in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.&nbsp; </FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our strategic plan is built upon extensive knowledge of current industry, consumer and market trends, and is formulated to differentiate the Company.&nbsp;The strategic plan includes long-term initiatives to increase revenues and earnings, improve productivity and cost efficiencies of our Military, Food Distribution and Retail business segments, and leverage our corporate support services.&nbsp; The Company has strategic initiatives to improve working capital, manage debt, and increase shareholder value through capital expenditures with acceptable returns on investment.&nbsp; Several important elements of the strategic plan include:</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<UL style="MARGIN-TOP: 0in; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0in" type=disc>

<LI style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">Supply chain services focused on supporting our business segments with warehouse management, inbound and outbound transportation management and customized solutions for each business segment;</FONT>

<LI style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">Growing the Military segment through acquisition and expansion of&nbsp;<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">our distribution network</FONT>, as well as creating warehousing and transportation cost efficiencies;</FONT>

<LI style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">Providing our independent retail customers with a high level of order fulfillment, broad product selection including leveraging the </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">Our Family&#174;</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">and </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">Nash Brothers Trading Company&#8482;&nbsp;</FONT></I>brands, support services emphasizing best-in-class offerings in marketing, advertising,merchandising, store design and construction, market research, retail store support, retail pricing and license agreement opportunities; and </FONT>

<LI style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">Retail formats designed to appeal to the needs of today&#8217;s consumers.</FONT> </LI></UL>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; During fiscal 2012, we continued expansion activities associated with our Military business, including the integration of our new facility in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma into our distribution network during the first quarter of 2012, as well as transferring the operations of our Military distribution center in Jessup, Maryland to a larger facility in Landover, Maryland during the third quarter of 2012.&nbsp; We also expanded our Retail segment, with the acquisition of twelve Bag &#8216;N Save&#174; supermarkets located in Omaha and York, Nebraska during the second quarter of 2012, and the acquisition of eighteen No Frills&#174; supermarkets located in Nebraska and western Iowa during the third quarter of 2012.&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT size=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Additional description of our business is found in Part II, Item 7 of this report.</FONT></FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Military Segment</FONT></B></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Our Military segment sells and distributes grocery products primarily to U.S. military commissaries and exchanges.&nbsp; We are the largest distributor, by revenue, in this market.&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">On December 1, 2009, we purchased a facility in Columbus, Georgia, which began servicing military commissaries and exchanges in the third quarter of fiscal 2010.&nbsp; During the third quarter of fiscal 2010, we purchased a facility in Bloomington, Indiana and two adjacent facilities in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma for expansion of our Military business.&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The Bloomington, Indiana facility became operational during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2010, while the renovated Oklahoma City, Oklahoma facility became operational during the first quarter of fiscal 2012. &nbsp;During the third quarter of fiscal 2012, we transferred the operations of our Military distribution center in Jessup, Maryland to a larger facility in Landover, Maryland.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The products we distribute are delivered to 174 military commissaries and over 400 exchanges located in 37 states across the United States and the District of Columbia, Europe, Puerto Rico, Cuba, the Azores, Egypt and Bahrain.&nbsp; Our distribution centers are strategically located among the largest concentration of military bases in the areas we serve and near Atlantic ports used to ship grocery products to overseas </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">commissaries and exchanges. <FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 115%; FONT-SIZE: 11pt" lang=EN-US><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">Our Military <FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">segment </FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">has</FONT></FONT><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"> an </FONT>outstanding reputation as a distributor focused on U.S. military commissaries and exchanges, based in large measure on our excellent service metrics, which include fill rate, on-time delivery and shipping accuracy. </FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT size=2></FONT>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt">

<FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">
<A href="#TABLEOFCONTENTS">Table of Contents</A></FONT></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt">&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The Defense Commissary Agency, also known as DeCA, operates a chain of commissaries on U.S. military installations throughout the world.&nbsp; DeCA contracts with manufacturers to obtain grocery and related products for the commissary system.&nbsp; Manufacturers either deliver the products to the commissaries themselves or, more commonly, contract with distributors such as us to deliver the products.&nbsp; Manufacturers must authorize the distributors as their official representatives to DeCA, and the distributors must adhere to DeCA&#8217;s frequent delivery system procedures governing matters such as product identification, ordering and processing, information exchange and resolution of discrepancies.&nbsp; We obtain distribution contracts with manufacturers through competitive bidding processes and direct negotiations.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">We have approximately&nbsp;600</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> distribution contracts with manufacturers that supply products to the DeCA commissary system and various exchange systems.&nbsp; These contracts generally have an indefinite term, but may be terminated by either party without cause upon 30 days prior written notice to the other party.&nbsp; The contracts typically specify the commissaries and exchanges we are to supply on behalf of the manufacturer, the manufacturer&#8217;s products to be supplied, service and delivery requirements and pricing and payment terms</FONT><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">.&nbsp; </FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Our ten largest manufacturer customers represented approximately 39% of the Military segment&#8217;s fiscal 2012 sales.</FONT><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp; &nbsp;</FONT></B></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; As commissaries need to be restocked, DeCA identifies each manufacturer with which an order is to be placed for additional products, determines which distributor is the manufacturer&#8217;s official representative for a particular commissary or exchange location, and places a product order with that distributor under the auspices of DeCA&#8217;s master contract with the applicable manufacturer.&nbsp; The distributor selects that product from its existing inventory, delivers it to the commissary or commissaries designated by DeCA, and bills the manufacturer for the product shipped.&nbsp; The manufacturer then bills DeCA under the terms of its master contract.&nbsp; Overseas commissaries are serviced in a similar fashion, except that a distributor&#8217;s responsibility is to deliver products as and when needed to the port designated by DeCA, which in turn bears the responsibility for shipping the product to the applicable commissary or overseas warehouse.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; After we ship a particular manufacturer&#8217;s products to commissaries in response to an order from DeCA, we invoice the manufacturer for the product price plus a service and or drayage fee that is typically based on a percentage of the purchase price, but may in some cases be based on a dollar amount per case or pound of product sold.&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">Our order handling and invoicing activities are facilitated by a procurement and billing system developed specifically for the military business, which addresses the unique aspects of its business, and provides our manufacturer customers with a web-based, interactive means of accessing critical order, inventory and delivery information.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Food Distribution Segment</FONT></B></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Our Food Distribution segment sells and distributes a wide variety of nationally branded and private label grocery products and perishable food products from 13 distribution centers to approximately 1,500 independent retail locations and corporate-owned retail stores located in 31 states across the United States.&nbsp; Our customers are relatively diverse with the largest customer, excluding our corporate-owned stores, consisting of a consortium of stores representing 6.4%, and the next largest customer representing 5.0% of our fiscal 2012 food distribution sales.&nbsp; No other customer represents greater than 5.0% of our food distribution business.&nbsp; Our ten largest independent customers represented approximately 37% of the Food Distribution segment&#8217;s fiscal 2012 sales.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our distribution centers are strategically located to efficiently serve our independent customers and our corporate-owned stores.&nbsp; The distribution centers are equipped with modern materials handling equipment for receiving, storing and shipping merchandise and are designed for high volume operations at low unit costs.&nbsp; We continue to implement operating initiatives to enhance productivity and expand profitability while providing a higher level of service to our distribution customers.&nbsp; Our distribution centers have varying levels of available capacity giving us enough flexibility to service additional customers by leveraging our existing fixed cost base, which can enhance our profitability.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Depending upon the size of the distribution center and the profile of the customers served, our distribution centers typically carry a full line of national brand and private label grocery products and perishable food products.Non-food items and specialty grocery products are distributed from two of our distribution centers located in Bellefontaine, Ohio and Sioux Falls, South Dakota.&nbsp; We currently operate a fleet of tractors and semi-trailers that deliver the majority of our products to our customers.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our retailers order their inventory at regular intervals through direct linkage with our information systems.&nbsp;Our Food Distribution sales are made on a market price plus fee and freight basis,with the fee based on the type of commodity and quantity purchased.&nbsp;We adjust our selling prices based on the latest market information, and our freight policy contains a fuel surcharge clause that allows us to mitigate the impact of rising fuel costs.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Products</FONT></I></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We primarily sell and distribute nationally branded products and a number of unbranded products, principally meat and produce, which we purchase directly from various manufacturers, processors and suppliers or through manufacturers&#8217; representatives and brokers.&nbsp; We also sell and distribute high quality private label products under the proprietary trademark </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Our Family</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#174;, a long-standing brand of Nash Finch that offers an alternative to national brands.&nbsp; In addition, we sell and distribute a premium line of branded products under the </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Nash Brothers Trading Company&#8482;</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> trademark, a lower priced line of private label products under the </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Value Choice&#174;</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> trademark and private label products for two of our independent customer groups.&nbsp; We offer over 3,700 stock-keeping units of competitively priced, high quality grocery products and perishable food products which compete with national branded and other value brand products. </FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Services&nbsp;</FONT></I></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 6pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; To further strengthen our relationships with our food distribution customers, we offer, either directly or through third parties, a wide variety of support services to help them develop and operate stores, as well as compete more effectively.&nbsp; These services include: </FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 6pt 0.75in"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face=symbol>&#183;</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 7pt" lang=EN-US face="times new roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">promotional, advertising and merchandising programs; </FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 6pt 0.75in"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face=symbol>&#183;</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 7pt" lang=EN-US face="times new roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">retail equipment procurement assistance; </FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: -0.25in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 6pt 0.75in"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face=symbol>&#183;</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 7pt" lang=EN-US face="times new roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">providing contacts for accounting, budgeting and payroll services;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 35.25pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">As of the end of fiscal 2012 and 2011, 62% and 60% of Food Distribution revenues, respectively, were from customers with whom we had entered into long-term supply agreements or from our corporate-owned retail stores. The length of our long-term supply agreements typically ranges from 5 to 7 years. These agreements also may contain provisions that give us the opportunity to purchase customers&#8217; independent retail businesses before being offered to any third party. </FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 35.25pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 35.25pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">We also provide financial assistance to our food distribution customers, primarily in connection with new store development or the upgrading and expansion of existing stores.&nbsp; As of December 29, 2012, we</FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> had loans, net of reserves, of $28.3 million </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">outstanding to 42 of our food distribution customers, and had guaranteed outstanding lease obligations of certain food distribution customers in the amount of $1.4 million.&nbsp; We also, in the normal course of business, sublease retail properties and assign retail property leases to third parties.&nbsp; As of December 29, 2012, the present value of our maximum contingent liability exposure, with respect to the subleases and assigned leases was $15.1 million and $8.3 million, respectively.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We distribute products to independent stores that carry the </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">IGA&#174;<SUP> 1 </SUP></FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">banner and our proprietary </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Food Pride&#174;</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> banner.&nbsp; We encourage our independent customers to join one of these banner groups to receive many of the same marketing programs and procurement efficiencies available to grocery store chains while allowing them to maintain their flexibility and autonomy as independents.&nbsp; To use either of these banners, these independents must comply with applicable program standards.&nbsp; As of December 29, 2012, we served 95</FONT><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> </FONT></B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">retail stores under the </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">IGA&nbsp;</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> banner and 42 retail stores under our </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Food Pride</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> banner.&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Retail Segment</FONT></B></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our Retail segment is made up of 75 corporate-owned grocery stores, located primarily in the Upper Midwest, in the states of Colorado, Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota and Wisconsin. &nbsp;Our corporate-owned stores principally operate under the&nbsp;<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Family Fresh Market&#174;,</FONT></I>&nbsp;</FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Sun Mart&#174;,</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Econofoods&#174;</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">,&nbsp;<I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Bag &#8216;N Save&#174;,&nbsp;No Frills&#174;,</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</FONT>&nbsp;</FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">AVANZA&#174;</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">, </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Family Thrift Center&#174;</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">, </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Pick &#8216;n Save&#174;, Prairie Market&#8482;</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">, </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Wholesale Food Outlet&#8482;,</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> and <I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Germantown Fresh Market&#8482;&nbsp; </FONT></I>banners.&nbsp;Our stores are typically located close to our distribution centers in order to create certain operating and logistical efficiencies.&nbsp; During the second quarter of 2012, we acquired twelve Bag &#8216;N Save&#174; supermarkets located in Omaha and York, Nebraska.&nbsp; During the third quarter of 2012, we acquired eighteen No Frills&#174; supermarkets located in Nebraska and western Iowa.&nbsp; This expansion of the Retail segment, including the addition of one store in the fourth quarter of 2012, was offset by the sale of two stores </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">since the end of fiscal 2011.&nbsp; </FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT size=2></FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our&nbsp;grocery stores offer a wide variety of high quality grocery products and services.&nbsp; Many have specialty departments such as fresh meat counters, delicatessens, bakeries, pharmacies, banking services and floral departments. The stores also provide services such as check cashing, fax services and money transfers.&nbsp;We emphasize outstanding customer service and have created our G.R.E.A.T. (Greet, React, Escort, Anticipate and Thank) Customer Service Program to train every associate (employee) on the core elements of providing exceptional customer service.&nbsp; &#8220;</FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The&nbsp;</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Fresh Place&#174;</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#8221; concept within our grocery stores is an umbrella banner that emphasizes our high quality perishable products, such as fresh produce, deli, meats, seafood, baked goods and takeout foods for today&#8217;s busy consumer.&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT size=2></FONT><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Competition</FONT></B></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Military Segment</FONT></I></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We are one of&nbsp;five</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> distributors with annual sales into the DeCA commissary system in excess of $100 million that distributes products via the frequent delivery system.&nbsp; The remaining distributors that supply DeCA tend to be smaller, regional and local providers.&nbsp; In addition, manufacturers contract with others to deliver certain products, such as baking supplies, produce, deli items, soft drinks and snack items, directly to DeCA commissaries and service exchanges.&nbsp; Because of the narrow margins in this industry, it is of critical importance for distributors to achieve economies of scale, which is typically a function of the density or concentration of military bases within the geographic market(s) a distributor serves, and the distributor&#8217;s share of that market.&nbsp; As a result, no single distributor in this industry, by itself, has a nationwide presence.&nbsp; Rather, distributors tend to concentrate on specific regions, or areas within specific regions, where they can achieve critical mass and utilize warehouse and distribution facilities efficiently.&nbsp; In addition, distributors that operate larger non-military specific distribution businesses tend to compete for DeCA commissary business in areas where such business would enable them to more efficiently utilize the capacity of their existing distribution centers.&nbsp; We believe the principal competitive factors among distributors within this industry are customer service, price, operating efficiencies, reputation with DeCA and location of distribution centers.&nbsp; We believe our competitive position is very strong with respect to all these factors within the geographic areas where we compete.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Food Distribution Segment </FONT></I></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The Food Distribution segment is highly competitive as evidenced by the low margin nature of the business. &nbsp;Success in this segment is measured by the ability to leverage scale in order to gain pricing </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">advantages and operating efficiencies, to provide superior merchandising programs and services to the independent customer base and to use technology to increase distribution efficiencies.&nbsp; We compete with local, regional and national food distributors, as well as with vertically integrated national and regional chains using a variety of formats, including supercenters, supermarkets and warehouse clubs that purchase directly from suppliers and self-distribute products to their stores.&nbsp; We face competition from these companies on the basis of price, quality, variety, availability of products, strength of private label brands, schedules and reliability of deliveries and the range and quality of customer services.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Continuing our quality service by focusing on key metrics such as our on-time delivery rate, fill rate, order accuracy and customer service is essential in maintaining our competitive advantage. &nbsp;During fiscal 2012, our distribution centers had an on-time delivery rate, defined as being within &#189; hour of our committed delivery time, of 97.6%; and a fill rate, defined as the percentage of cases shipped relative to the number of cases ordered, of 96.6%.&nbsp; We believe we are an industry leader with respect to these key metrics.&nbsp; </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;</FONT></I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Retail Segment&nbsp; </FONT></I><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"><BR></P></FONT></I>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our Retail segment is highly competitive.&nbsp; We compete with many organizations of various sizes, ranging from national and regional chains that operate a variety of formats (such as supercenters, supermarkets, extreme value food stores and membership warehouse club stores) to local grocery store chains and privately owned unaffiliated grocery stores.&nbsp; Although our target geographic&nbsp;<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">markets</FONT> have a relatively low presence of national and multi-regional grocery store chains, we face competition from supercenters and regional chains in most of these <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">markets</FONT>.&nbsp;Depending upon the market, we compete based on price, quality and assortment, store appeal (including store location and format), sales promotions, advertising, service and convenience.&nbsp; We believe our ability to provide convenience, outstanding perishable execution and exceptional customer service are particularly important factors in achieving competitive success. </FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Vendor Allowances and Credits</FONT></B></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; We participate with our vendors in a broad menu of promotions to increase sales of products.&nbsp; These promotions fall into two main categories, off-invoice allowances and performance-based allowances, and are often subject to negotiation with our vendors.&nbsp; In the case of off-invoice allowances, discounts are typically offered by vendors with respect to certain merchandise purchased by us during a specified period of time.&nbsp; We use off-invoice allowances to support a variety of marketing programs such as reduced price offerings for specific time periods, food shows, pallet promotions and private label promotions.&nbsp; The discounts are either reflected directly on the vendor invoice, as a reduction from the normal wholesale prices for merchandise to which the allowance applies, or we are allowed to deduct the allowance as an offset against the vendor&#8217;s invoice when it is paid.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In the case of performance-based allowances, the allowance or rebate is based on our completion of some specific activity, such as purchasing or selling product during a certain time period.&nbsp; This basic performance requirement may be accompanied by an additional performance requirement such as providing advertising or special in-store promotions, tracking specific shipments of goods to retailers (or to customers in the case of our own retail stores) during a specified period (retail performance allowances), slotting (adding a new item to the system in one or more of our distribution centers) and merchandising a new item, or achieving certain minimum purchase quantities.&nbsp; The billing for these performance-based allowances is normally in the form of a &#8220;bill-back&#8221; in which case we are invoiced at the regular price with the understanding that we may bill back the vendor for the requisite allowance when the performance is satisfied.&nbsp; We also assess an administrative fee, reflected on the invoices sent to vendors, to recoup our reasonable costs of performing the tasks associated with administering retail performance allowances.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">We collectively plan promotions with our vendors and arrive at the amount the respective vendor plans to spend on promotions with us.&nbsp; Each vendor has its own method for determining the amount of promotional funds to be spent with us.&nbsp; In most situations, the vendor allowances are based on units we purchased from the vendor.&nbsp; In other situations, the allowances are based on our past or anticipated purchases and/or the anticipated performance of the planned promotions.&nbsp; Forecasting promotional expenditures is a critical part of our frequently scheduled planning sessions with our vendors.&nbsp; As individual promotions are completed and the associated billing is processed, the vendors track our promotional program execution and spend rate, and discuss the tracking, performance and spend rate with us on a regular basis throughout the year.&nbsp; These communications include discussions with respect to future promotions, product cost, targeted retails and price <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">points, anticipated volume, promotion expenditures, vendor maintenance, billing issues and procedures, new items/discontinued items, and trade spend levels relative to budget per event and per year, as well as the resolution of any issues that arise between the vendor and us.&nbsp; In the future, the nature and menu of promotional programs and the allocation of dollars among them may change as a result of our ongoing negotiations and commercial relationships with our vendors.</FONT></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT size=2></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: -4.5pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; TEXT-INDENT: 0in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">Available Information</FONT></B></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; caption.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"><A name="RISKFACTOR"></A>ITEM 1A.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </FONT></B><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">RISK FACTORS</FONT></I></B></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">In addition to the other information in this Form 10-K, you should carefully consider the specific risk factors set forth below in evaluating Nash Finch because any of the following risks could materially affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and future prospects.&nbsp; </FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">We face substantial competition, and our competitors may have added resources, which could place us at a competitive disadvantage and adversely affect our financial performance</FONT></I></B><B><I><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; TEXT-TRANSFORM: uppercase; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">.&nbsp;</FONT></I></B></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: justify; PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; TEXT-TRANSFORM: uppercase; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Our businesses are highly competitive and are characterized by high inventory turnover, narrow profit margins and increasing consolidation.&nbsp; Our Food Distribution and Military businesses compete not only with local, regional and national food distributors, but also with vertically integrated national and regional chains that employ a variety of formats, including supercenters, supermarkets and warehouse clubs. Our Retail business, focused in the Upper Midwest, has historically competed with traditional grocery stores and is increasingly competing with alternative store formats such as supercenters, warehouse clubs, dollar stores and extreme value food stores<FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">, as well as non-traditional retailers such as discount stores, pharmacies, and convenience stores.</FONT></FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Some of our Food Distribution and Retail competitors are substantially larger and may have greater financial resources and geographic scope, lower merchandise acquisition costs and lower operating expenses than we do, thereby intensifying price competition at the wholesale and retail levels.&nbsp; Industry consolidation and the </FONT><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">expansion of alternative store formats, which have gained and continue to gain market share at the expense of traditional grocery stores, tend to produce even stronger competition for our Retail business and for the independent customers of our Food Distribution business.&nbsp; To the extent our independent customers are acquired by our competitors or are not successful in competing with other retail chains and non-traditional competitors, sales by our Food Distribution business will also be affected.&nbsp; If we fail to effectively implement strategies to respond to these competitive pressures, our operating results could be adversely affected by price reductions, decreased sales or margins, or loss of market share.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The Military segment faces competition from large national and regional food distributors as well as smaller food distributors.&nbsp; Due to the narrow margins in the military food distribution industry, it is of critical importance for distributors to achieve economies of scale, which are typically a function of the density or concentration of military bases in the geographic markets a distributor serves and a distributor's share of that market.&nbsp; As a result, no single distributor in this industry, by itself, has a nationwide presence.</FONT></P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; TEXT-TRANSFORM: uppercase; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Our businesses are</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> sensitive to changes in overall economic conditions that impact consumer spending, including discretionary spending </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">and buying habits</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">.&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Economic downturns or uncertainty have adversely affected overall demand and intensified price competition, but also have caused consumers to "trade down" by purchasing lower margin items and to make fewer purchases in traditional supermarket channels.&nbsp; Continued negative</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> economic conditions affecting disposable consumer income such as employment levels, business conditions, changes in housing market conditions, the availability of credit, interest rates, volatility in fuel and energy costs, </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">food price inflation or deflation, employment trends in our markets affecting wage and income levels</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">, the impact of natural disasters or acts of terrorism, and other matters affecting consumer spending could cause consumers to shift even more of their spending to lower-priced competitors.&nbsp; General reductions in the level of discretionary spending or continued shifts in consumer discretionary spending to our competitors could adversely affect our growth and profitability.</FONT></P>

A general slowdown in economic activity caused by an extended period of economic uncertainty could adversely affect our businesses.&nbsp;Difficult financial and economic conditions could also adversely affect our customers&#8217; ability to meet the terms of sale or our suppliers&#8217; ability to fully perform their commitments to us. </FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US color=black face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The impact of events in foreign countries which could result in increased political instability and social unrest and the economic ramifications of significant budget deficits in the United States and changes in policy attributable to them at both the federal and state levels could adversely affect our businesses and customers.&nbsp;Adverse economic or geopolitical events could potentially reduce our access to or increase prices associated with products sourced abroad.&nbsp;Such adverse events could lead to significant increases in the price of the products we procure, fuel and other supplies used in our business, utilities, or taxes that cannot be fully recovered through price increases.&nbsp;In addition, disposable consumer income could be affected by these events, which could have a negative impact on our results of operations and financial condition.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 12pt 0in 0pt" align=justify><B><I><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Our businesses could be negatively affected if we fail to retain existing customers or attract significant numbers of new customers.</FONT></I></B></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 12pt 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Growing and increasing the profitability</FONT><FONT style="TEXT-TRANSFORM: uppercase; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">of our distribution businesses is dependent in large measure upon our ability to retain existing customers and capture additional distribution customers through our existing network of distribution centers, enabling us to more effectively utilize the fixed assets in those businesses.&nbsp; Our ability to achieve these goals is dependent, in part, upon our ability to continue to provide a high level of customer service, offer competitive products at low prices, maintain high levels of productivity and efficiency, particularly </FONT><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">in the process of integrating new customers into our distribution system, and offer marketing, merchandising and ancillary services that provide value to our independent customers.&nbsp; If we are unable to execute these tasks effectively, we may not be able to attract significant numbers of new customers, and attrition among our existing customer base could increase, either or both of which could have an adverse impact on our revenue and profitability.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 12pt 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Because our Military segment sells and distributes grocery products to military commissaries and exchanges in the U.S. and overseas, any material changes in the commissary system, the level of governmental funding to DeCA, military staffing levels, or the locations of bases may have a corresponding impact on the sales and operating performance of this segment.&nbsp; These changes could include privatization of some or all of the military commissary system, relocation or consolidation of commissaries and exchanges, base closings, troop redeployments or consolidations in the geographic areas containing commissaries and exchanges served by us, or a reduction in the number of persons having access to the commissaries and exchanges.&nbsp; Mandated reductions in government expenditures, including those imposed as a result of sequestration, may impact the level of funding to DeCA and could have a material impact on our operations.</FONT></P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; TEXT-TRANSFORM: uppercase; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Our Retail segment faces competition from regional and national chains operating under a variety of formats that devote square footage to selling food (i.e., supercenters, supermarkets, extreme value stores, membership warehouse clubs, dollar stores, drug stores, convenience stores, various formats selling prepared foods, and other specialty and discount retailers), as well as from independent food store operators in the markets where we have retail operations.&nbsp; </FONT><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Our strategic initiatives for the Retail segment are designed to create value within our organization.&nbsp; These initiatives include designing and reformatting our retail stores to increase overall retail sales performance.</FONT><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> In connection with these efforts, there are numerous risks and uncertainties, including our ability to successfully identify which course of action will be most financially advantageous for each retail store, our ability to identify those initiatives that will be the most effective in improving the competitive position of our retail stores in the markets they operate in, our ability to implement these initiatives efficiently and in a timely manner, and the response of competitors to these initiatives.&nbsp; If we are unable to improve the overall competitive position of our retail stores, the operating performance of that segment may decline, and we may need to recognize additional impairments of our long-lived assets and goodwill, close or sell underperforming stores, and incur restructuring or other charges to our earnings associated with such closure and disposition activities.&nbsp; In addition, we cannot make assurances that we will be able to replace any of the revenue our Food Distribution operations derive from stores that are closed or sold.</FONT></P>

Assumptions underlying estimates of expected revenue growth </FONT><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">or overall cost savings may not be met or economic conditions may deteriorate.&nbsp; Customer acceptance of new retail formats we develop may not be as anticipated, hampering our ability to attract new retail customers or maintain our existing retail customer base.&nbsp; Additionally, our management may have its attention diverted from other important activities while trying to execute new strategic initiatives.&nbsp; If these or other factors limit our ability to execute our strategic initiatives, our expectations of future results of operations, including expected revenue growth and cost savings, may not be met.</FONT></P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; TEXT-TRANSFORM: uppercase; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Efforts to grow our business may include acquisitions.&nbsp; The successful integration of newly acquired businesses is dependent on our ability to identify suitable candidates for acquisition, effect acquisitions at acceptable rates of return, obtain adequate financing, and negotiate acceptable terms and conditions.&nbsp; Our success also depends in a large part on our ability to successfully integrate such operations and personnel in a timely and efficient manner while retaining the customer base of the acquired operations.&nbsp; If we cannot identify suitable acquisition candidates, successfully integrate these operations and retain the customer base, we may experience material adverse consequences to our results of operations and financial condition.&nbsp; The integration of separately managed businesses operating in different markets involves a number of risks, including the following:</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; TEXT-TRANSFORM: uppercase; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: -9pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 27pt"><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; TEXT-TRANSFORM: uppercase; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: -9pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 27pt" align=justify><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#8226; difficulties in the assimilation of different corporate cultures and business practices, such as those involving vendor promotions, and of geographically dispersed personnel and operations;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: -9pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 27pt"><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; TEXT-TRANSFORM: uppercase; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: -9pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 27pt"><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; TEXT-TRANSFORM: uppercase; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: -9pt; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt 27pt" align=justify><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&#8226; expenses of any undisclosed liabilities, such as those involving environmental or legal matters.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; TEXT-TRANSFORM: uppercase; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Successful integration of newly acquired operations, including our purchases of twelve Bag &#8216;N Save&#174; supermarkets during the second quarter of fiscal 2012 and eighteen No Frills&#174; supermarkets during the third quarter of fiscal 2012 will depend on our ability to manage those operations, fully assimilate the operations into our Retail business segment, realize opportunities for revenue growth presented by strengthened product offerings and expanded geographic market coverage, maintain the customer base and eliminate redundant and excess costs.&nbsp; We may not realize the anticipated benefits or savings from these new operations in the time frame anticipated, if at all, or such benefits and savings may include higher costs than anticipated.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><B><I><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Substantial operating losses may occur if the customers to whom we extend credit or for whom we guarantee loan or lease obligations fail to repay us.</FONT></I></B></P>

<P style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: avoid; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; TEXT-TRANSFORM: uppercase; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In the ordinary course of business, we extend credit, including loans, to our food distribution customers, and provide financial assistance to some customers by guaranteeing their loan or lease obligations.&nbsp; We also lease store sites for sublease to independent retailers.&nbsp; Generally, our loans and other financial accommodations are extended to small businesses that are unrated and may have limited access to conventional financing.&nbsp; As of December 29, 2012, we had loans, net of reserves, of $28.3 million outstanding to </FONT><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">42&nbsp;</FONT><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> of our food distribution customers and had guaranteed outstanding lease obligations of food distribution customers totaling $1.4 million.&nbsp; In the normal course of business, we also sublease retail properties and assign retail property leases to third parties.&nbsp; As of December 29, 2012, the present value of our maximum contingent liability exposure, with respect to subleases and assigned leases was $15.1 million and $8.3 million, respectively.&nbsp; While we seek to obtain security interests and other credit support in connection with the financial accommodations we extend, such collateral may not be sufficient to cover our exposure.&nbsp; Greater than expected losses from existing or future credit extensions, loans, guarantee commitments or sublease arrangements could negatively and potentially materially impact our operating results and financial condition.</FONT></P>

Although we have an off-site disaster recovery center and have installed security programs and procedures, security could be compromised and technology failures and systems disruptions could occur.&nbsp; This could result in a loss of sales or profits or cause us to incur significant costs, including payments to third parties for damages.</FONT><FONT style="LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt; TEXT-TRANSFORM: uppercase; LETTER-SPACING: -0.1pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> &nbsp;</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Severe weather conditions and natural disasters could damage our properties and adversely impact the geographic areas where we conduct our business.&nbsp; Severe weather and natural disasters could also affect the suppliers from whom we procure products and could cause disruptions in our operations and affect our supply chain capabilities. &nbsp;In addition, unseasonably adverse climatic conditions that impact growing conditions and the crops of food producers may adversely affect the availability or cost of certain products. </FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Unions may attempt to organize our employees.</FONT></I></B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> &nbsp;</FONT></I></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">While our management believes that our employee relations are good, we cannot be assured that we will not experience pressure from labor unions or become the target of campaigns similar to those faced by our competitors.&nbsp; We have always respected our employees&#8217; right to unionize or not to unionize.&nbsp; However, the unionization of a significant portion of our workforce could increase our overall costs at the affected locations and adversely affect our flexibility to run our business in the most efficient manner to remain competitive or acquire new business.&nbsp; In addition, significant union representation would require us to negotiate wages, salaries, benefits and other terms with many of our employees collectively and could adversely affect our results of operations by increasing our labor costs or otherwise restricting our ability to maximize the efficiency of our operations. </FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0in; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0in" align=justify><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Costs related to a multi-employer pension plan, which has liabilities in excess of plan assets, may have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s financial condition and results of operations. </FONT></I></B></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The Company participates in the Central States Southeast and Southwest Areas Pension Funds (&#8220;CSS&#8221; or &#8220;the plan&#8221;), a multi-employer pension plan, for certain unionized employees.&nbsp; The Company&#8217;s contributions to the plan may escalate in future years should we withdraw from the plan or due to factors outside the Company&#8217;s control, including the bankruptcy or insolvency of other participating employers, actions taken by trustees who manage the plan, government regulations, or a funding deficiency in the plan.&nbsp; Escalating costs associated with the plan may have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s financial condition and results of operations.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">CSS adopted a rehabilitation plan as a result of its actuarial certification for the plan year beginning January 1, 2008 which placed the plan in critical status. &nbsp;The Actuarial Certification of Plan Status as of January 1, 2011 certified that the Central States Pension Fund remains in critical status with a funded percentage of 58.9%. &nbsp;The plan adopted an updated rehabilitation plan effective December 31, 2010 which implements additional measures to improve the plan&#8217;s funded level, including establishing an increased minimum retirement age and actuarially adjusting certain pre-age 65 benefits for participants who retire after July 1, 2011. &nbsp;Despite these changes, we can make no assurances of the extent to which the updated rehabilitation plan will improve the funded status of the plan.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Effective July 9, 2009, the trustees of CSS formalized a decision to terminate the participation of YRC Worldwide, Inc. (formerly Yellow Freight and Roadway Express, &#8220;YRC&#8221;) and USF Holland, Inc. from the pension fund.&nbsp; Under an agreement between the Teamsters and YRC dated September 24, 2010, which was eventually ratified by the membership, YRC resumed participation in the plan effective June 1, 2011 at a reduced contribution rate.&nbsp; At this time, there is no change to the funding obligations due from other </FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">participating employers in the fund as a result of this agreement; however, further developments may necessitate a reevaluation of the funding obligations at some point in the future.<BR></FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-INDENT: 0.5in; MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">The underfunding of the plan is not a direct obligation or liability of the Company, however, it is possible that the Company&#8217;s contributions to the plan may increase in future years as a result of the plan&#8217;s funding status.&nbsp;The amount of any potential increase in contributions would depend upon several factors, including the number of employers contributing to the plan, results of the Company&#8217;s collective bargaining efforts, investment returns on assets held by the plan, actions taken by the trustees of the plan, and actions that the Federal government may take.&nbsp; Moreover, if the Company were to exit certain markets or otherwise cease making contributions to the plan, the Company could trigger a substantial withdrawal liability. &nbsp;We are currently unable to reasonably estimate such liability.&nbsp; Any adjustment for withdrawal liability will be recorded when it is probable that a liability exists and can be reasonably estimated.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Increases in employee benefit costs and other labor relations issues may lead to labor disputes and disruption of our businesses.</FONT></I></B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT></I></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; If we are unable to control health care costs, other wage and benefit costs, or gain operational flexibility under our collective bargaining agreements, we may experience increased operating costs and an adverse impact on future results of operations. &nbsp;There can be no assurance that the Company will be able to negotiate the terms of any expiring or expired agreement in a manner that is favorable to the Company. &nbsp;Therefore, potential work disruptions from labor disputes could result, which may affect future revenues and profitability. </FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">We are subject to the risk of product liability claims, including claims concerning food and prepared food products.</FONT></I></B></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></I></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The sale of food and prepared food products for human consumption may involve the risk of injury.&nbsp; Injuries may result from tampering by unauthorized third parties, product contamination or spoilage, including the presence of foreign objects, substances, chemicals, other agents, or residues introduced during the growing, storage, handling and transportation phases.&nbsp; We cannot be sure that consumption of products we distribute and sell will not cause a health-related illness in the future or that we will not be subject to claims or lawsuits relating to such matters. </FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Negative publicity related to these types of concerns, or related to product contamination or product tampering, whether valid or not, might negatively impact demand for products we distribute and sell, or cause production and delivery disruptions.&nbsp; We may need to recall products if any of these products become unfit for consumption. Costs associated with these potential actions could adversely affect our operating results. </FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">Threats or potential threats to security may adversely affect our business.</FONT></I></B><I><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"> &nbsp;</FONT></I></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt" align=justify><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Threats or acts of terror, data theft, information espionage, or other criminal activity directed at the food industry, the transportation industry, or computer or communications systems, including security measures implemented in recognition of actual or potential threats, could increase security costs and adversely affect our operations. </FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><B><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"></FONT></B>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0in 0in 0pt"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman"><FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt" lang=EN-US face="Times New Roman">On February 26, 2013, the Nash Finch Board of Directors declared a cash dividend of $0.18 per common share, payable on March 22, 2013, to stockholders of record as of March 8, 2013.</FONT></FONT></P>
